text:
marie: FYI after yesterday's int3 sweep for the new code-focused model variant I'm seeing a reproducible drop on code-fidelity slices (function signatures and inline code blocks) in our deid-code-rag holdout. Not massive but concerning: missing parentheses, truncated code blocks, and subtle tokenization splits causing wrong variable names. Need a microgolden of code examples + labeler checklist.

tomas: oh no. can you drop the eval metrics? which slices?

marie: pasted quick run:

```
$ rbin eval --model codeq-1.0-int3 --dataset deid-code-rag --slices code_blocks,fn_sig,inline_snippets
Exact-token-preserve: 88.3% (-5.5% vs fp16)
Signature-match: 90.1% (-4.2%)
Identifier-split-errors: 3.8% (+2.9%)
Hallucination-rate: 5.2% (+1.7%)
Latency p50: 245ms
```

ivy: hmm. do we think this is quant rounding on embedding/pos-enc weights or a tokenizer alignment issue? any cfg changes in serving?

marie: serving was default. I tried forcing bpe-legacy tokenizer in a local run and identifier-split errors dropped 1.1%. So tokenizer/quant interplay seems plausible. Also observed failure modes where backtick-delimited blocks are split across tokens that int3 ops mishandle.

tomas: treat as a quality regression. assemble microgolden focused on code blocks: 400 candidates -> dedupe -> final 250. Labeler checklist must include exact-code-preserve, signature-check, variable-name-check, hallucination-note. 3 labelers per sample.

labeler-bot: New ticket ML-4333 created: "codeq int3: code-fidelity regression on deid-code-rag". Labeling plan attached.

marie: proposed microgolden schema:
- 250 code examples (mix of short funcs ~20-80 tokens and long snippets up to 1200 tokens) pulled from recent RAG sessions (deid-filtered).
- 80 examples with multi-line fenced blocks and mixed markdown+code.
- 70 examples containing inline math/code (LaTeX/markdown) to test delimiting.
- 100 synthetic adversarial perturbations that change spacing/backtick placement and variable casing.
- Label fields: exact_code_preserve (yes/no), signature_match (yes/no), identifier_split (yes/no), hallucination_flag (yes/no), severity (0-3), evidence_span (short).

ivy: assembly/dedupe plan: sample 1k recent candidates -> run byte-level fuzzyhash dedupe + tokenizer-shingle dedupe (shingle size=5) -> surface 400 for prelabel QA -> labeler queue LB-9001. I'll attach provenance: source_ts, session_id, tokenizer_version, md5_text, bpe_hash.

marie: labeler instructions text (ops copy):
"When labeling, run the model output against the provided source code. Confirm the output reproduces the same tokens for identifiers, punctuation, and block delimiters. If a token is split or renamed (e.g., my_var -> my_ var), mark identifier_split and include the smallest evidence span. For hallucinations (new code or explanations not present in source), mark hallucination_flag and add a short note. Escalate any unmasked secrets to privacy-ops immediately."

ops-bot: Labeling batch created: LB-9001. ETA first pass 48-72 hrs.

tomas: parallel action: we need a tokenizer+quant matrix sweep logged. Nora (cc), can you run a small grid: int3 with bpe-legacy vs bpe-v2, and per-layer exceptions (keep embeddings fp16), kernel variants (aten,flash) and kv-cache on/off. Example: 

```
rbin quant-sweep --model codeq-1.0 --bits 3 --tokenizer bpe-legacy,bpe-v2 --layer-exceptions embeddings --kernels aten,flash --kv-cache on,off --eval deid-code-rag --save ML-4333/logs
```

ivy: will kick off dedupe+assembly now and push artifacts to ML-4333/artifacts. I'll also include a small script that computes tokenizer-shingle mismatch rate.

marie: if we find a tokenizer/quant combo that recovers fidelity we can either pin tokenizer or add a runtime override on Dedicated for code-heavy routes. Also consider an Optimize profile 'code-int3' recommending embeddings fp16 + bpe-legacy.

tomas: console: add a dashboard card tracking 'code-exact-token-preserve' for golden and production slices, with a weekly alert if it drops >3%.

marie: agreed. I'll file the console ticket and attach example promptset once LB-9001 has first pass.

ivy: dedupe started. will ping when LB-9001 is populated.

labeler-bot: ML-4333 updated: logs path attached, LB-9001 created.

marie: action items recap: (1) ivy assemble + dedupe + populate LB-9001, (2) nora run tokenizer+quant sweep and save logs to ML-4333, (3) labelers start LB-9001, (4) marie file console card + Optimize profile suggestion. Ping in-thread for blockers. :rocket:
